likely_cause: The Firebase configuration file is missing from the Android app module.
aliases: google services plugin could not find configuration
fix: Select your Firebase project and register your Android application using its application ID.
Place it inside the app/ directory of your Android project.
Verify that the Google Services Gradle plugin is configured.
Sync Gradle and rebuild the Android project.
verification: Sync Gradle and rebuild the project. Confirm that the processDebugGoogleServices task completes successfully.

likely_cause: A dependency may be unavailable, repositories may be missing, dependency coordinates may be incorrect, or network access may be blocked.
fix: Check the dependency coordinates and version.
Verify repositories such as google() and mavenCentral() are configured.
Check network access and proxy settings.
Verify that the dependency is available in the configured repositories.
verification: Run a Gradle sync and confirm that dependency resolution succeeds.

likely_cause: The referenced symbol may be missing, incorrectly imported, unavailable in the current module, or not included in dependencies.
fix: Check the spelling and capitalization of the symbol.
Check whether the required import is present.
Verify that the required dependency is included.
Confirm that the dependency version supports the API.
Check whether the symbol belongs to a different module.
verification: Rebuild the project and check whether the unresolved reference is gone.
